newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslems outraged over US policy paper.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslems outraged over US policy paper.

text.p: Bosnian Moslem leaders expressed outrage on Thursday over a U.S. policy paper on the disputed town of Brcko, saying that a possible decision to award the area to the Serbs would be a grave "injustice".

Sarajevo politicians and press were in an uproar over an internal policy paper written by U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum, which suggested giving the strategic town to Bosnia's Serb republic.
Political leaders said the paper cast doubt on the legitimacy of this month's arbitration hearings in Rome which are supposed to settle differences over Brcko.
"If a political decision is going to be reached, then the arbitration is a farce," Hasan Muratovic, the newly-appointed foreign trade minister in the central government, told Reuters.
Another Moslem official said the proposal, if carried out, would reward "war crimes and genocide" and provoke widespread anger among ordinary people.
The official also alleged it was clear that the United States and other major powers would determine the outcome of the arbitration process, not legal arguments.
"The tragedy is the decision will be reached by the (major powers') contact group and not the arbiter," he said.
Sarajevo newspapers shared the same sense of cynicism. The daily Dnevni Avaz led its front page with the headline, "Games around Brcko" and another paper asked, "Brcko to the Serbs?!"
The main Moslem political party, the SDA, issued a stern warning that hinted at resorting to military action over Brcko.

"If we deviate from the arbitration in a legal sense and avoid a just solution for Brcko...and bearing in mind that genocide was committed in Brcko, the SDA will draw certain conclusions and correct a possible injustice," said the Party of Democratic Action.
An American lawyer, Roberts Owen, chairs the three-member arbitration panel which was scheduled to finish its hearings on Thursday.
If the panel -- Owen and Moslem and Serb representatives -- fails to come to an agreement, Owen has the right to deliver a final verdict. The arbitration panel faces a February 15 deadline.
The narrow Brcko land corridor, which connects Serb- controlled territory to the west and east, is the country's most volatile flashpoint.
The Bosnian Serbs, who seized the area at the beginning of the conflict in 1992, have repeatedly threatened to go to war over Brcko and Moslem leaders have returned the threat.
U.S. peace negotiators failed to reach a settlement for Brcko in November 1995 and left it up to arbitration.
Moslem-Croat federation officials confirmed accounts from European diplomats about the contents of the policy paper.
They said Washington had not necessarily made up its mind on the explosive Brcko question. "This might be some sort of trial balloon," said a federation official.

Diplomats said Kornblum's paper set out various options for resolving Brcko, including international administration. But they said the document favoured awarding the northern town to the Serb republic while allowing a transit route for the Moslem-Croat federation.
